description:
pkix-ct/Cargo.toml:31: 'log-list = ["dep:sha2"]' — the log-list feature gates sha2 because CtLogList::insert verifies SHA-256(key_der) == log_id.

But verify.rs uses sha2::{Digest, Sha256} unconditionally (verify.rs:60 'use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};' is at module level) for merkle_leaf_hash (line 697), inner_hash (line 678), and issuer_key_hash_from_cert (line 1013). verify.rs itself is gated by the 'log-list' feature (lib.rs:48-49 has 'mod verify' under cfg(feature = log-list)), so sha2 happens to be available — but only because of the log-list feature gate, not as an explicit dependency.

This creates an implicit dependency on log-list: 'I want SCT verification but not log-list management' is impossible. The feature combos compiling correctly is accidental — anyone refactoring this could easily break it.

Suggested fix: pull sha2 out of log-list's optional dep set; make it a required dependency (always pulled in), since the crate's core verification path needs it. Then log-list gates only the CtLog/CtLogList types, not the hash crate. Document that sha2 is always required.

Alternatively: split into 'sct-verify' and 'log-list' features where sct-verify gates sha2 and verify.rs, and log-list builds on top. But pre-1.0 the simpler 'sha2 is always present' route is more honest.
title: Cargo.toml 'log-list' feature pulls in sha2 unconditionally — sha2 is also used by verify.rs but not gated
